reel.hook: Your cheque bounced? Watch the clock.

slides.title: Send a notice in 30 days
slides.body: Within 30 days of the bank's return memo, send the drawer a written notice demanding the cheque amount.

slides.title: 15 days to pay
slides.body: The drawer has 15 days from receiving your notice to pay. If they pay, the matter can end there.

slides.title: Then one month to file
slides.body: If still unpaid, file a complaint under Section 138 within one month. Punishment can be up to 2 years' jail or twice the cheque amount.

caption_linkedin:
A bounced cheque is not just a banking hiccup. Under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, it can be a criminal offence, but the payee must act within strict timelines:

• Send a written demand notice to the drawer within 30 days of receiving the bank's return memo
• The drawer has 15 days from receiving the notice to pay
• If payment is not made, the complaint should be filed within one month after that 15-day period ends
• Cheques must be presented within their validity, currently 3 months from the date on the cheque
• Punishment can extend to 2 years' imprisonment, a fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both

Missing a deadline can weaken the case, so businesses and individuals should track these dates carefully. For help with a notice or complaint, you can consult a Bar Council-verified advocate on AdvocateSetu: https://advocatesetu.com
